en: Thereafter, while guarding the maṇḍala according to the procedure to be described (the maṇḍala-vidhi), she sits upon the ground of the maṇḍala which has been marked out with lines according to the dimensions of the maṇḍala. Having prepared a fragrant mandala in the center and visualized the Earth Goddess Vasundharā as being present, she contemplates three *hūṃ* syllables on the moon of her right hand. Then, by striking the ground three times with the tips of her fingers, through those sounds and the rays of light from the *hūṃ* syllables—

Having worshipped with the offering of water for the feet (*argha*) and other rites the Earth Goddess—who has arisen from the exhortation, become one with the Knowledge Being (*jñānasattva*), her heart bound with joy, yellow in color, gentle, wearing white garments, adorned with all ornaments, holding a *bhadraghaṭa* vessel and displaying the gesture of fearlessness with her two hands (the left and the other), single-faced, and standing before him—one should do so with great devotion.

Following that, one should prepare the base by means of a mandala for drawing and marking lines, in accordance with the mandala as it will be explained through the ritual procedures; then, having fashioned a fragrant maṇḍala and visualized the Earth Goddess arising from the syllable *pāṃ*, one should contemplate three *hūṃ*s upon a moon disc in the right hand.

She strikes the surface of the earth three times with the tips of her fingers; through the sound of that and the light rays of the syllable *hūṃ*, she is perfectly exhorted and emerges as the Earth Goddess, who has become one with the wisdom-being (*jñānasattva*). She is yellow in color, possesses a joyful mind, is peaceful, wears white garments, and is adorned with all ornaments.

To her who stands before him, having one face and two arms, holding a *bhadraghaṭa* (auspicious vase) with her left hand and displaying the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) with the other, he makes perfect offerings preceded by the water for the feet and so forth.
Immediately thereafter: Oṃ ehy ehi mahādevi pṛthivī lokamātare | Sarvaratnasusaṃpūrṇe divyālaṃkārabhūṣite ||
O you whose sound is the resonance of necklaces and anklets, who are fully worshipped by Vajrasattva!
Having taken this *argha* offering, accomplish the rites of the mandala!
Hrīḥ hrīḥ hrīḥ hrīḥ haṃ svāhā!

oṃ. Come, come, O great goddess of the earth, mother of the world, completely filled with all jewels, adorned with excellent ornaments, possessing the sound of necklaces and anklets, who perfectly worships Vajrasattva! Having accepted this water for offering, please bring this maṇḍala to perfect accomplishment! hrīḥ hi hi hi haṃ svāhā.
Reciting this three times, one should perform the consecration (adhivāsana).
Having recited this three times, one should perform the consecration.
Having said, "Let it be done in this very way," one should contemplate her as having dissolved right there. Thus ends the ritual procedure for the consecration of the earth (vasundharādhivāsana).
Thus concludes the ritual for the special consecration of the Earth Goddess.
